Sharing the two samples or querying Gy at x_t changes the recorded procedure.

variants.cost: Per iteration: one Gx call, one sequential Gy call, two independent sample draws and two vector updates. T iterations use T calls to each partial-gradient oracle and 2T draws. Sampling and estimator arithmetic costs are unspecified. Full-gradient calls must not silently be charged as partial-gradient calls. No function values, inner maximization or g* evaluation is required.
variants.implementation_details_ref: p.5 Algorithm 1 lines 1–6; Eq.(2) exact deterministic specialization
variants.name: Algorithm 1 Stoc-AGDA
variants.output: No explicit return instruction is printed. A finite T truncation exposes (x_T,y_T), matching the iterate pairs assessed in Eq.(3); no accuracy stopping certificate is asserted.
public_inputs: Initial pair (x0,y0) in R^d1 x R^d2
Positive sequences {tau1^t},{tau2^t}, distribution P and estimators Gx,Gy
Caller-selected finite iteration budget T when needed
variants.query_and_update: At t=0,1,2,... draw xi_t1,xi_t2 i.i.d. from P, fresh each iteration. Query Gx(x_t,y_t,xi_t1); set x_{t+1}=x_t-tau1^t Gx(x_t,y_t,xi_t1). Then query Gy(x_{t+1},y_t,xi_t2); set y_{t+1}=y_t+tau2^t Gy(x_{t+1},y_t,xi_t2).
variants.requirements: Execution requires partial-gradient estimators at the displayed points and fresh independent samples. Assumption 3 requires E[Gx(x,y,xi)]=grad_x f(x,y), E[Gy(x,y,xi)]=grad_y f(x,y), each expected squared error <=sigma^2. Assumptions 1–2 and two-sided PL concern performance, not execution.
variants.state_and_initialization: Start with supplied (x0,y0); no auxiliary estimator, projection, inner solve or warm start is specified.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Algorithm 1 allows positive step sequences and specifies an infinite loop without a stopping test. Theorem 3.1 prints constant steps 0<tau2<=1/ell and 0<tau1<=mu2^2 tau2/(18ell^2), requiring valid public ell,mu2; this is source tuning, not an accepted performance guarantee. Finite T truncation is a caller convention.
